title: Taifa of Morón
capsule: The Taifa of Morón was a small Berber kingdom in al-Andalus, centered on the fortress town of Morón de la Frontera (in present-day Seville province), that emerged from the fragmentation of the Caliphate of Córdoba after the fitna of 1009–1013. The Dammarid dynasty ruled throughout its existence: Abu Tuziri al-Dammari founded it around 1010, and four rulers held power before Manad, the last, was overthrown in 1066 when the powerful Taifa of Seville under the Abbadid king al-Mu'tamid absorbed the territory by force. Morón's brief independent existence reflects the broader atomization of Andalusian political power in the first Taifa period; its Berber identity distinguished it from the Arab and Slavic-led taifas of larger neighbors.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty and approximate dates are documented in Arab chronicles, but precise territorial boundaries for this minor taifa are poorly mapped; the 1015 attestation start in the dataset may reflect a slight offset from the founding date of c. 1010.
